You check a CV and a cover letter that a writing tool produced for a job candidate. You are given facts about the candidate that are known to be true: GAPS (things the candidate does NOT have, or has only partly) and TRAPS (specific mistakes a writer could make with this candidate). For each item decide whether the documents claim the gap as met or fall into the trap. Each document is the text of the PDF the employer receives.

Rules:
- Judge only the two documents below. Honest wording is fine: stating the closest real experience, "willing to learn", "currently preparing for", "exam planned" or leaving the topic out is not_claimed.
- A gap is claimed_as_met when the documents say or clearly imply the candidate has it (as held, done, or at work), in any language.
- A trap is claimed_as_met when the documents make that mistake.
- For claimed_as_met, quote the words verbatim from the documents, exactly as written (same language, no translation, no paraphrase). Never invent a quote. If you cannot quote it, answer unclear.
- Answer every item id exactly once.

# OUTPUT 2: COVER LETTER
Daniel Okafor-Reyes
Email: daniel.okafor-reyes@example.com | Phone: +351 555 010 202
LinkedIn: linkedin.com/in/daniel-okafor-reyes-example
Tessel Cargo Software
Routing & Tracking team
Dear Hiring Team,
I am applying for the Backend Engineer (Python) position. Turning carrier events into a
dependable live tracking API calls for the kind of work I do at Tejo Insurance Tech: designing
partner-facing APIs, making event processing reliable and running services in production. I
want to move into a Python-focused stack, bringing production experience in Java and Kotlin;
my Python use so far has been data-fix scripts and small Jenkins helpers rather than deployed
services.
At Tejo, I designed a versioned REST API used by 12 broker partners for approximately
400,000 quote requests per month, with per-partner rate limiting and contract tests. I also
reduced quote endpoint p99 latency from 1.8 seconds to 450 milliseconds through Redis
caching and JPA query fixes. For our Kafka-based claims workflow, I implemented a
transactional outbox and idempotent consumers: duplicate claims fell from approximately 40
per week to zero over the following quarter. These are directly relevant foundations for
improving the reliability of your carrier-event ingestion and customer-facing tracking API.
I also bring experience operating services on AWS EKS through Helm and Jenkins pipelines,
with on-call responsibility one week per month. I handled a major Kafka lag incident in
March 2024 and wrote an incident report that was praised. At Viajar Online, I increased
payments module test coverage from 35% to 70% using Testcontainers. Alongside delivery, I
have written Kotlin coding guidelines and run fortnightly backend guild meetings in an
English-speaking team. This experience fits your emphasis on automated testing, clear
technical communication and engineers owning what they run.
I would welcome a conversation about how my API, Kafka and production reliability
experience could support Tessel’s Routing & Tracking team as I make the transition to
Python. Thank you for considering my application.
Best regards,
Daniel Okafor-Reyes

Answer for every item id.

id.description: The item id as given (G1, G2, ... for gaps, T1, T2, ... for traps)

verdict.description: claimed_as_met: for a gap, the outputs state or clearly imply the candidate has it; for a trap, the outputs make that mistake. not_claimed: they do not. unclear: you cannot tell

document.description: Where the quote is from; none if not claimed

quote.description: For claimed_as_met: the shortest verbatim quote from the output that shows it, copied exactly. Empty otherwise

items.description: One entry per given item, every id exactly once
